slides.title: What is a Pattern? 🎨
slides.text: A pattern is a sequence of shapes or colours that follows a rule! The same small group comes back again and again in the exact same order!
slides.spoken: A pattern is a sequence of shapes or colours that follows a rule! The same small group comes back again and again in the exact same order!

slides.title: The Unit of Repeat 🔄
slides.text: The smallest block that repeats to build the whole pattern is called the unit of repeat! In red, blue, red, blue, the unit is red and blue!
slides.spoken: The smallest block that repeats to build the whole pattern is called the unit of repeat!

slides.title: Extending Patterns ➡️
slides.text: To extend a pattern, you find the unit of repeat and copy it again and again! After red and yellow comes red, then yellow!
slides.spoken: To extend a pattern, you find the unit of repeat and copy it again and again!

slides.title: Daily Life Patterns 🏠
slides.text: Patterns are everywhere around us! Floor tiles, sari borders, necklaces, and even the days of the week from Monday to Sunday follow repeating patterns!
slides.spoken: Patterns are everywhere around us! Floor tiles, sari borders, necklaces, and days of the week follow repeating patterns!

slides.title: Simple Graphs & Charts 📊
slides.text: A graph is a picture that shows information clearly! On a bar graph, the tallest bar shows the most popular item, and the shortest bar shows the least!
slides.spoken: A graph is a picture that shows information clearly! The tallest bar shows the most, and the shortest bar shows the least!

challenges.question: What comes next in the pattern: Red, Blue, Red, Blue, Red, ___?
challenges.hint: Look at the repeating pair: Red, Blue! After Red comes...?
challenges.misconception: The unit is Red-Blue! After Red, the next item in the repeating pair is always Blue!

challenges.question: What is the UNIT OF REPEAT in: Circle, Square, Triangle, Circle, Square, Triangle...?
challenges.hint: Find the shortest block that repeats without missing any shape!
challenges.misconception: The unit must include all shapes in order! Circle, Square, Triangle is the smallest block that rebuilds the whole pattern!

challenges.question: Drag the right beads to extend the pattern: Red, Yellow, Red, Yellow, Red, ___, ___
challenges.hint: The unit is Red-Yellow! Keep repeating Red then Yellow!
challenges.misconception: Always copy the full unit in order! After Red comes Yellow, then Red again!

easierVariant.hint: Take it slow. The unit is Red-Yellow! Keep repeating Red then Yellow!

challenges.question: On a bar graph of favourite fruits, what does the TALLEST bar show?
challenges.hint: Tallest bar means highest number of votes! Which fruit did the most children choose?
challenges.misconception: The tallest bar always shows the item with the most votes (most popular)! The shortest bar shows the least!

challenges.question: Complete the repeating pattern: Star, Star, Circle, Star, Star, Circle, Star, ___, ___
challenges.hint: The unit is Star-Star-Circle! After one Star, what comes next?
challenges.misconception: The unit is three items long: Star, Star, Circle! After a single Star, you need another Star and then a Circle!

easierVariant.hint: Take it slow. The unit is Star-Star-Circle! After one Star, what comes next?

challenges.question: Which of these is a valid repeating pattern from daily life?
challenges.answer: Floor tiles: Square, Triangle, Square, Triangle
options: Floor tiles: Square, Triangle, Square, Triangle
challenges.hint: A pattern has a regular repeating order, like alternating floor tiles!
challenges.misconception: Floor tiles alternate in a strict repeating order! Random scattered leaves have no fixed unit of repeat.

interactiveObjects.label: Floor tiles: Square, Triangle, Square, Triangle

challenges.question: Arrange the sequence of days in a weekly repeating cycle!
challenges.hint: Monday comes first in the school week! What comes after Monday?
challenges.misconception: Days of the week follow a fixed cycle: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday, then it repeats!

easierVariant.hint: Take it slow. Monday comes first in the school week! What comes after Monday?

challenges.question: Favourite Fruits Graph: Apple has 5 votes (tallest), Mango 4, Banana 3, Orange 2 (shortest). Which fruit has the LEAST votes?
challenges.hint: Look for the shortest bar on the graph! Shortest bar = least votes.
challenges.misconception: The shortest bar represents the fewest votes (least popular)! Here Orange has only 2 votes, making it the shortest bar.
